title: Telemetry-based stability scoring and guardrails for regional routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a stability score per region that combines streaming latency percentiles (p50, p95), transient spike damping, packet-level network health markers (loss, rtt variance), and adapter error rates to inform the region selector. Score drives: primary region selection, tiered routing decisions (hosted -> dedicated -> private), and automatic model-variant fallbacks when a region's stability drops below configured thresholds. The system must be explainable, tunable per-customer tier, and safe to roll out with gradual traffic migration and quick rollback.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic stability score computed every minute for each region with components: weighted p50, weighted p95, network-loss-penalty, error-rate-penalty, and recent-trend multiplier
Score smoothing that avoids flip-flop for short-lived spikes (configurable hysteresis and cool-down window)
Routing decision module consumes scores and provides ranked region candidates with reasons for selection (score breakdown) visible in Console
Canary rollout plan validated on internal dev account with 5% traffic shift and automated rollback on >10% increase in user-facing errors
Unit/integration tests and load tests demonstrating correct scoring under synthetic spike, slow drift, and network partition scenarios
Dashboard and alerting: Grafana panel with score decomposition and a PagerDuty alert when a region’s score drops >0.35 from baseline for 15 minutes
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Initial spike-damping algorithm draft complete (exponential decay + percentile windowing). Documented math and rationale in Confluence.
2026-02-20: Telemetry schema change submitted - added fields for rtt_variance and tcp_retransmit_count to region metrics. Telemetry team reviewed; changes accepted. See PR telemetry#412.
2026-02-28: Prototype scoring service implemented in routing sandbox. Local end-to-end validation with replayed PROD traces shows reduced noisy failovers vs naive p95-only approach.

2026-03-05: Design review with PM and SRE. Key feedback: need per-tenant thresholds, and a safe default for specialized private deployments. Action: add customer-tier config and a hard-pref fallback policy for private deployments.

2026-03-10: Integration tests added for model-variant fallback (quantized variant) when region score < threshold. Observability hooks added for per-request reason codes. Preparing canary run for 2026-W10.
decisions: Use a composite score: 0.5*p95_normalized + 0.3*p50_normalized + 0.15*network_loss_penalty + 0.05*error_rate_penalty. Rationale: preserve latency tail signal while incorporating noise-resistant central tendency and explicit network health.
Apply exponential smoothing with alpha=0.25 and a separate short-term buffer for spike detection. This enables fast detection of true degradations while avoiding immediate flapping.
Expose per-customer tier overrides: enterprise customers may opt for higher sensitivity (lower hysteresis) and stricter private fallback policies.

Model-variant fallback order: full-precision -> aggressively-quantized -> CPU-offload stub. Fallback chosen only when region score persists below threshold for configured duration and capacity checks pass.
Operator-visible reason codes included in routing responses: SCORE_OK, SCORE_LOW_P95, SCORE_NET_LOSS, SCORE_RECENT_DRIFT. This helps debugging and postmortem analysis.
Do not automatically re-route traffic out of private deployments unless explicit admin opt-in; allow local policy to decide.
Rollout via feature flag gated canary: default disabled for existing customers; enabled for internal dev orgs and a small set of opt-in customers.
Fallback decision is composable with existing hysteresis and circuit-breaker mechanisms; the stability score feeds the circuit-breaker input rather than replacing it.
